record.context_brief: Prime and special values in explicit sequences
record.original_question: For integers a and b with gcd(a,b)=1, determine how many prime values occur in the sequence a p_n + b, where p_n is the nth prime, and ask analogously how many terms are of the form n! or n^n. Ask the same questions for sequences of the form a n + b with a in {+1,0}, and for the sequences k^k + 1 and k^k - 1.

evidence.quote: If (a, b) = 1, how many primes does the progression apn + b ... contain? ... Same questions for an + b ... Same questions for kk + 1 and kk - 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime number (so $p_1=2$, $p_2=3$, $p_3=5$, ...). For integers $a,b$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $a\ge 1$, consider the sequence
$$S_{a,b} := \{\,a p_n + b : n \ge 1\,\}.$$

(i) Determine how many terms of $S_{a,b}$ are themselves prime numbers; in particular, decide for which pairs $(a,b)$ the set of primes in $S_{a,b}$ is infinite, and (when infinite) give an asymptotic for the counting function.

(ii) Determine how many terms of $S_{a,b}$ are of the form $m!$ for some positive integer $m$.

(iii) Determine how many terms of $S_{a,b}$ are of the form $m^m$ for some positive integer $m$.

Ask the same three questions for the arithmetic progression
$$T_{a,b} := \{\,a n + b : n \ge 1\,\}, \qquad a\in\{0,1\},\ \gcd(a,b)=1,$$
and for the two sequences
$$U^+ := \{\,k^k + 1 : k\ge 1\,\}, \qquad U^- := \{\,k^k - 1 : k\ge 1\,\}.$$

In particular, decide whether each of $U^+$ and $U^-$ contains infinitely many primes, and whether either contains infinitely many factorials or terms of the form $m^m$.
artifact.status_search_result: These are classical and largely open problems. Counting primes of the form $a p_n + b$ is closely related to the still-unsolved twin-prime and de Polignac conjectures (the case $a=1$, $b=2$). The infinitude of primes of the form $k^k+1$ or $k^k-1$ is also a well-known open problem; only finitely many such primes are known and no infinitude result exists. Dirichlet's theorem fully resolves the prime count in $an+b$ for $a\ge 1$, but the factorial and $m^m$ versions are open.

status_evidence.title: de Polignac's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: For every positive even number n, there are infinitely many prime gaps of size n. The case n=2 is the twin prime conjecture. The conjecture remains unproven.
status_evidence.claim: Whether $p_n+b$ is prime infinitely often for general even $b$ is open.

status_evidence.title: Prime k^k+1 / k^k-1 (OEIS A100208 / related)
status_evidence.snippet: Only a handful of primes of the form k^k ± 1 are known; whether infinitely many exist is an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Infinitude of primes in $k^k\pm1$ is unresolved.
